newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space crews celebrate Thanksgiving.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space crews celebrate Thanksgiving.

text.p: U.S. astronauts, orbiting in separate spacecraft, will dine on special, if not entirely traditional, meals to celebrate Thanksgiving.

For five astronauts aboard the space shuttle Columbia, irradiated turkey steaks, stuffing, cranberry sauce and pumpkin-coloured frosted cakes are on the menu, but their meal will have to wait until a 6 1/2-hour space walk ends early Friday.
"When we get back inside, believe me, we'll be hungry for that Thanksgiving turkey," astronaut Tom Jones, one of two space walkers, told NASA Administrator Daniel Goldin on Tuesday.

"We've got some off the shelf, supermarket, room temperature stabilised turkey dinners that we'll be digging into right after I get that helmet off. We'll all be anxious to have a meal together after that hard day's work."
"You didn't make it sound too appetising," Goldin replied, laughing.
"One has to make do with the resources at hand," Jones explained.
Columbia's crew had expected to be home before Thanksgiving, but the shuttle's 16-day mission was delayed by booster rocket problems and bad weather.
Aboard Russia's space station Mir, astronaut John Blaha, 73 days into a four-month mission, will also tuck into a turkey dinner,
"I have some turkey," he told NBC in an interview from space on Wednesday. "It's not my favourite food here. My favourite... is actually a couple of Russian dishes that are just outstanding."
After more than a year of training in Russia, Blaha admitted his palette has come to prefer the Russian staple of meat, potatoes and vegetables.
Although he will miss this year's traditional family get together, Blaha said he still had a lot to be thankful for.
"I have quite an outstanding view of the cosmos and the planet from up here, so for this Thanksgiving that's what I'll have," he said.
The former Vietnam fighter pilot will also spend the Christmas holiday away from home. Blaha is not due to return to earth until January when the space shuttle Atlantis visits Mir to pick him up.
